title: How wheels came to suitcases: early patents, Bernard Sadow (1970) and Robert Plath's Rollaboard (1987)

sources.title: The History of the Humble Suitcase
'Tis the season to covet twenty indispensable luxuries for those who travel enough to call airports home (1996-12-23)

facts.text: A wheeled trunk was patented in 1887 and a wheeled suitcase in 1945, but neither caught on.
Bernard Sadow, a luggage company executive, got the idea for a wheeled suitcase while struggling with two heavy suitcases at an airport in Puerto Rico.
At that airport, Sadow saw a worker easily moving heavy machinery on a platform with wheels.
Sadow fixed four small wheels to the bottom of a suitcase and added a strap so it could be pulled along.
Department stores in New York at first refused Sadow's suitcase, saying nobody would pull luggage on wheels.
Macy's began selling Sadow's wheeled suitcase in 1970; his patent was granted in 1972.
Sadow's four-wheeled design, towed on a strap, was not the form that later became standard.
In 1987 Robert Plath, a Northwest Airlines pilot, created the Rollaboard: an upright bag with two wheels and a handle that folds away.
By the mid-1990s, wheeled bags of this type were widely used by airline crews in airports.
The upright, two-wheeled bag with a retractable handle became the model for most modern carry-on luggage.
